elements.requirement: A person to whom section 4 of the Bail Act 1976 applies must be granted bail except as provided in Schedule 1 to the Act.
elements.quote: shall be granted bail except as provided in Schedule 1 to this Act

elements.requirement: Section 4 of the Bail Act 1976 applies to a person who is accused of an offence when that person appears or is brought before a magistrates’ court or the Crown Court in the course of or in connection with proceedings for the offence.
elements.quote: appears or is brought before a magistrates’ court or the Crown Court in the course of or in connection with proceedings for the offence

elements.requirement: Section 4 of the Bail Act 1976 applies to a person who is accused of an offence when that person applies to a court for bail or for a variation of the conditions of bail in connection with the proceedings.
elements.quote: applies to a court for bail or for a variation of the conditions of bail in connection with the proceedings

elements.requirement: Section 4(2) of the Bail Act 1976 does not apply with respect to proceedings on or after a person’s conviction of the offence.
elements.quote: does not apply as respects proceedings on or after a person’s conviction of the offence

elements.requirement: Section 4 of the Bail Act 1976 applies to a person whose extradition is sought in respect of an offence when that person appears or is brought before a court in the course of or in connection with extradition proceedings in respect of the offence.
elements.quote: he appears or is brought before a court in the course of or in connection with extradition proceedings in respect of the offence

elements.requirement: Section 4 of the Bail Act 1976 applies to a person whose extradition is sought in respect of an offence when that person applies to a court for bail or for a variation of the conditions of bail in connection with the proceedings.
elements.quote: he applies to a court for bail or for a variation of the conditions of bail in connection with the proceedings

elements.requirement: Section 4(2A) of the Bail Act 1976 does not apply if the person whose extradition is sought is alleged to have been convicted of the offence.
elements.quote: does not apply if the person is alleged to have been convicted of the offence

elements.requirement: Section 4 of the Bail Act 1976 applies to a person who, having been convicted of an offence, appears or is brought before a magistrates’ court or the Crown Court under Schedule 4 to the Sentencing Code (referral orders: referral back to appropriate court), Schedule 5 to that Code (breach of reparation order), Schedule 7 to that Code (breach, revocation or amendment of youth rehabilitation orders), Part 2 of Schedule 10 to that Code (breach of requirement of community order), or the Schedule to the Street Offences Act 1959 (breach of orders under section 1(2A) of that Act).
elements.quote: having been convicted of an offence, appears or is brought before a magistrates’ court or the Crown Court

elements.requirement: Section 4 of the Bail Act 1976 applies to a person who has been convicted of an offence and whose case is adjourned by the court for the purpose of enabling inquiries or a report to be made to assist the court in dealing with that person for the offence.
elements.quote: whose case is adjourned by the court for the purpose of enabling inquiries or a report to be made to assist the court in dealing with him for the offence

elements.requirement: Schedule 1 to the Bail Act 1976 has effect in respect of conditions of bail for a person to whom section 4 applies.
elements.quote: Schedule 1 to this Act also has effect as respects conditions of bail for a person to whom this section applies

elements.requirement: In Schedule 1 to the Bail Act 1976, 'the defendant' means a person to whom section 4 applies.
elements.quote: “the defendant” means a person to whom this section applies

elements.requirement: In Schedule 1 to the Bail Act 1976, any reference to a defendant whose case is adjourned for inquiries or a report means a person to whom section 4 applies by virtue of section 4(4).
elements.quote: reference to a defendant whose case is adjourned for inquiries or a report is a reference to a person to whom this section applies by virtue of subsection (4) above

elements.requirement: Section 4 of the Bail Act 1976 is subject to section 41 of the Magistrates’ Courts Act 1980 regarding the restriction of bail by a magistrates’ court in cases of treason.
elements.quote: subject to section 41 of the Magistrates’ Courts Act 1980 (restriction of bail by magistrates’ court in cases of treason)

elements.requirement: Section 4 of the Bail Act 1976 is subject to section 115(1) of the Coroners and Justice Act 2009 regarding the requirement that bail decisions in murder cases be made by a Crown Court judge.
elements.quote: section 115(1) of the Coroners and Justice Act 2009 (bail decisions in murder cases to be made by Crown Court judge)

elements.requirement: Section 4 of the Bail Act 1976 is subject to section 25 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 regarding the exclusion of bail in cases of homicide and rape.
elements.quote: subject to section 25 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 (exclusion of bail in cases of homicide and rape)

elements.requirement: In taking any decisions required by Part I or Part II of Schedule 1 to the Bail Act 1976, the court must have regard, so far as relevant, to any misuse of controlled drugs by the defendant.
elements.quote: considerations to which the court is to have regard include, so far as relevant, any misuse of controlled drugs by the defendant

elements.requirement: For the purposes of section 4(9) of the Bail Act 1976, 'controlled drugs' and 'misuse' have the same meanings as in the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971.
elements.quote: “controlled drugs” and “misuse” having the same meanings as in the Misuse of Drugs Act 1971
